items.title: Sam Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: before I went to the west coast I was with Buddy Rich, with the small group.

ctx.x: That’s very diplomatic of you. Perhaps not. You even did, to backtrack just a touch, you did some gigs with Tommy Dorsey and a few of the big bands? © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

Oh yeah. I went on the road for about eight months with Shep Fields, I was playing alto and clarinet. And then I guess, who was on that band, Red Mitchell’s brother was playing bass on that band, but after I got off that, that was commercial. I guess my brother had been playing with Tommy Dorsey and he probably said hey my kid brother’s playing clarinet, maybe he could take a chance and try the thing. And I went there and Tommy was very nice. I wasn’t experienced at really reading like the charts, because the…
When you were doing the bar mitzvahs and the gigs to pay the rent, you were kind of expected to know a certain—
